μαγοσ.def: a sorcerer, a magician, a wizard.

μαγωγ.def: (Hebrew), Magog, sometimes as name of a people, sometimes as name of a country in the Old Testament, probably the Scythians; hence: used in apocalyptic literature.

μαδιαμ.def: (Hebrew), Midian, generally taken to mean or to include the peninsula of Sinai.

μαθητευω.gloss: I make disciples, make into disciples
μαθητευω.def: I make a disciple of, train in discipleship; pass: I am trained, discipled, instructed.

μαθουσαλα.def: (Hebrew) Methuselah, son of Enoch and father of Lamech.

μαινομαι.def: I am raving mad, speak as a madman.

μακαριζω.def: I bless, pronounce blessed or happy.

μακαρισμοσ.gloss: regarding as happy, blessed, or enviable
μακαρισμοσ.def: regarding as happy, blessed, or enviable.

μακεδονια.def: (Hebrew), Macedonia, a Roman province north of Achaia (Greece).

μακεδων.def: a Macedonian, an inhabitant of the Roman province Macedonia.

μακραν.def: at a distance, far away, remote, alien.

μακροθυμεω.gloss: I suffer long, have patience, am forbearing
μακροθυμεω.def: I suffer long, have patience, am forbearing, perseverance.

μακροσ.def: long, distant, far; of long duration.

μαλακοσ.def: (a) soft, (b) of persons: soft, delicate, effeminate.

μαλελεηλ.def: Mahalaleel or Maleleel, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

μαλχοσ.def: Malchus, a servant of the high-priest at Jerusalem.

μαναην.def: (Graecized form of Aramaic Menahem), Manaen, probably a member of Herod Antipas' court.

μανασσησ.def: (Hebrew), Manasseh, (a) son of Joseph, founder of a tribe of Israel, (b) son of Hezekiah and father of Amon (Amos).

μανθανω.def: I learn; with adj. or nouns: I learn to be so and so; with acc. of person who is the object of knowledge; aor. sometimes: to ascertain.

μαννα.def: (Hebrew), manna, the supernatural food eaten by the Israelites in the desert: of spiritual food.

μαντευομαι.def: I divine, practice soothsaying, suggesting the fraud involved in the practice.

μαραινω.def: pass: I die, wither (like the grass).

μαραν.def: (Aramaic), either: Our Lord hath come, or: Our Lord cometh (will come, is at hand).

μαρθα.def: Martha, sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany.

μαρια.def: Mary, Miriam, (a) the mother of Jesus, (b) of Magdala, (c) sister of Martha and Lazarus, (d) wife of Cleopas, (e) mother of John Mark, (f) a Christian woman in Rome.

μαρκοσ.def: Mark, who also had the Hebrew name John, son of Mary, nephew of Barnabas, coadjutor of Barnabas, Paul, and Peter.

μαρτυρεω.def: I witness, bear witness, give evidence, testify, give a good report.

μαρτυρομαι.gloss: I call to witness, testify, solemnly charge
μαρτυρομαι.def: (properly: I call (summon) to witness, and then absolutely) I testify, protest, asseverate; I conjure, solemnly charge.

μαρτυσ.def: a witness; an eye- or ear-witness.

μαστιγοω.def: I flog, scourge, the victim being strapped to a pole or frame; met: I chastise.

μαστιξ.def: (a) a scourge, lash, of leathern thongs with pieces of metal sewn up in them, (b) met: severe pains (sufferings), disease.

ματαιοσ.def: vain, unreal, ineffectual, unproductive; practically: godless.

ματαιοτησ.def: vanity, emptiness, unreality, purposelessness, ineffectiveness, instability, frailty; false religion.

ματαιοω.def: I become vain or foolish, am perverted.

ματην.def: in vain, in an unreal way, to no purpose.

μαχη.def: (earlier: a battle, conflict, hence) in the sphere of words, etc: strife, contention, quarrel.

μαχομαι.gloss: I engage in battle, fight, strive
μαχομαι.def: I engage in battle, fight; hence: I strive, contend, dispute.

μεγαλυνω.def: (a) I enlarge, lengthen, (b) I increase, magnify, extol.

μεγασ.def: large, great, in the widest sense.

μεγισταν.def: a great one, a lord; a courtier, satrap, nobleman.

μεθερμηνευω.def: I translate (from one language into another), interpret.

μεθιστημι.gloss: I move out of its place, transfer
μεθιστημι.def: I cause to change its place, move out of its place; I translate, transfer, remove.

μεθοδεια.def: (a way of search after something, an inquiry; a method), scheming, craftiness, deceit.

μεθυσκω.def: I make drunk; pass: I become drunk.

μεθυω.def: I am intoxicated with wine, am drunk.

μελεασ.def: Melea, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

μελει.gloss: it is a care, it concerns
μελει.def: it is a care, it is an object of anxiety, it concerns.

μελεταω.def: I devise, plan; practice, exercise myself in, study, ponder.

μελισσιοσ.def: belonging to bees, coming from bees.

μελλω.def: I intend, am about to; I delay, linger.

μελχι.def: Melchi, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

μελχισεδεκ.def: Melchizedek, king and priest of Salem.

μεμβρανα.def: a parchment leaf, perhaps for notes.

μεμψιμοιροσ.def: blaming one's lot or destiny, discontented, complaining.

μεν.def: an untranslatable particle, generally answered by "de", each of the two introducing a clause intended to be contrasted with the other.

μενω.def: I remain, abide, stay, wait; with acc: I wait for, await.

μεριζω.def: I divide into parts, divide, part, share, distribute; mid: I share, take part in a partitioning; I distract.

μεριμναω.def: I am over-anxious; with acc: I am anxious about, distracted; I care for.

μερισ.def: (a) a part, division of a country, (b) a share, portion.

μερισμοσ.def: (a) a distributing, a distribution, (b) a parting, dividing, severance, separation.

μεσημβρια.def: (lit: midday, hence, the position of the sun at midday), the South.

μεσιτησ.def: (a) a mediator, intermediary, (b) a go-between, arbiter, agent of something good.

μεσονυκτιον.def: midnight, the middle of the period between sunset and sunrise.

μεσοποταμια.def: Mesopotamia, the Country between the (two) Rivers, i.e. the Euphrates and the Tigris.

μεσοσ.def: middle, in the middle, between, in the midst of.

μεσοτοιχον.def: a middle wall, partition wall, barrier.

μεσουρανημα.def: mid-heaven, the middle of heaven, the zenith.

μεσοω.def: I am in the middle, am advanced midway.

μετα.def: (a) gen: with, in company with, (b) acc: (1) behind, beyond, after, of place, (2) after, of time, with nouns, neut. of adjectives.

μεταβαινω.gloss: I leave, depart, remove, pass over
μεταβαινω.def: I change my place (abode), leave, depart, remove, pass over.

μεταβαλλω.def: I change; mid: I change my mind.

μεταγω.gloss: I turn about, change the position of
μεταγω.def: (usually: transfer, transport, and met: to a better mind), I turn about, change the position of; pass: I am brought back.

μεταδιδωμι.def: (lit: I offer by way of change, offer so that a change of owner is produced), I share; sometimes merely: I impart, bestow.

μεταιρω.gloss: I change my position, depart, remove
μεταιρω.def: I change my position, depart, remove.

μετακαλεω.def: mid: I summon to myself, send for.

μετακινεω.def: trans: I move away, dislodge, remove.

μεταλαμβανω.def: (a) with gen: I take a share (part) of, share in, partake of, (b) with acc: I take after (later) or take instead.

μεταμελομαι.def: (lit: I change one care or interest for another), I change my mind (generally for the better), repent, regret.

μετανοεω.def: I repent, change my mind, change the inner man (particularly with reference to acceptance of the will of God), repent.

μετανοια.def: repentance, a change of mind, change in the inner man.

μετασχηματιζω.gloss: I change the outward appearance, transfigure, adapt
μετασχηματιζω.def: I change the outward appearance (the dress, the form of presentment) of something, transfigure; I adapt.

μετατιθημι.def: (a) I transfer, mid: I go over to another party, desert, (b) I change.

μετεχω.def: I have a share of, participate in, share, partake of, am a member of.

μετοικιζω.def: I transport, cause to migrate, remove.

μετρητησ.def: a measure, amphora, about 39.39 liters or 8.75 gallons.

μετριοπαθεω.gloss: I bear gently with, have compassion
μετριοπαθεω.def: I bear gently with, have compassion.

μετρον.def: a measure, whether lineal or cubic; a measuring rod.

μεχρι.def: as far as, until, even to.

μηδαμωσ.gloss: by no means, not at all
μηδαμωσ.def: by no means, not at all.

μηδοσ.def: a Mede, a Median, from east of Assyria.

μηνυω.def: (a) I reveal, make known (in a law court), I lay information, inform, (b) I make known, point out.

μηποτε.gloss: lest at any time, lest, perhaps
μηποτε.def: lest at any time, lest; then weakened: whether perhaps, whether at all; in a principal clause: perhaps.

μηπωσ.gloss: lest in any way, lest perhaps
μηπωσ.def: lest in any way, lest perhaps.

μητι.def: if not, unless, whether at all.

μητραλωασ.def: a matricide, smiter of his mother.

μιλητοσ.def: Miletus, a city on the coast of the Roman province Asia.

μιλιον.def: a Roman mile, measuring 1478.5 meters or 5820.9 feet.

μιμνησκομαι.def: I remember, call to mind, recall, mention.

μισεω.def: I hate, detest, love less, esteem less.

μισθαποδοσια.def: (lit: repayment of price or payment of price due), reward, due punishment.

μισθιοσ.def: a paid worker, hired servant, hireling (contrasted with a slave).

μισθοσ.def: (a) pay, wages, salary, (b) reward, recompense, punishment.

μισθοω.def: I hire out, mid: I hire, engage.

μιτυληνη.def: Mitylene, the capital of the island of Lesbos in the northern Aegean sea.

μνα.def: a mina, a Greek monetary unit equal to 100 drachma.

μνασων.def: Mnason, an early Christian, native of Cyprus, resident at a place between Caesarea and Jerusalem.

μνημονευω.def: I remember, hold in remembrance, make mention of.

μνηστευω.def: I ask in marriage; pass: I am betrothed.

μογγιλαλοσ.gloss: one speaking with difficulty, a stammerer
μογγιλαλοσ.def: one speaking with difficulty, a stammerer.

μοδιοσ.gloss: a dry measure, nearly two English gallons
μοδιοσ.def: a dry measure, nearly two English gallons.

μοιχαλισ.def: (a) an adulteress (that is, a married woman who commits adultery), (b) Hebraistically: extended to those who worship any other than the true God.

μοιχαομαι.def: I commit adultery, not only of a married woman but of a married man.

μοιχευω.def: I commit adultery (of a man with a married woman, but also of a married man).

μοιχοσ.def: an adulterer, that is, a man who is guilty with a married woman.

μολοχ.def: Moloch, a god worshipped by several Semitic peoples.

μολυνω.def: I soil, stain, pollute, defile, lit. and met.

μοσχοποιεω.gloss: I make a model of a calf
μοσχοποιεω.def: I make an image of a calf.

μουσικοσ.def: skilled in music; subst: a musician, singer.

μυεω.def: I initiate, instruct; pass: I am disciplined, learn (a lesson).

μυθοσ.def: an idle tale, fable, fanciful story.

μυκτηριζω.def: (properly: I turn up the nose as a sign of contempt), I sneer at, disdain.

μυλων.def: a mill-house, the place where grain was ground.

μυρα.def: Myra, a port in Lycia, south-west Asia Minor.

μυριασ.def: a myriad, group of ten thousand, a ten thousand.

μυριοι.def: ten thousand; also used for a very large number, innumerable.

μυσια.def: Mysia, a country in the north-west of the Roman province Asia (and of Asia Minor).

μυστηριον.def: a mystery, secret, of which initiation is necessary; in the NT: the counsels of God, once hidden but now revealed in the Gospel or some fact thereof; the Christian revelation generally; particular truths or details of the Christian revelation.

μυωπαζω.def: I am short-sighted, blink, see dimly.

μωλωψ.def: a bruise, stripe, left on the body by scourging.

μωμαομαι.def: I blame, find fault with, slander.

μωραινω.gloss: I make foolish, taint, make useless
μωραινω.def: (a) I make foolish, turn to foolishness, (b) I taint, and thus: I am tasteless, make useless.

μωροσ.def: (a) adj: stupid, foolish, (b) noun: a fool.

μωσησ.def: Moses; met: the books of Moses, the Pentateuch.
